ACADEMIC_ISLR_TEST.citation: James, Witten, Hastie, and Tibshirani, An Introduction to Statistical Learning, 7th printing, Chapter 2 and Chapter 5
ACADEMIC_ISLR_TEST.locator: Chapter 2 discussion of training error versus test error; Chapter 5 discussion of held-out observations and cross-validation
ACADEMIC_ISLR_TEST.supports: A test observation was not used in training; training error can underestimate test error; held-out data is used to assess generalization.
ACADEMIC_ISLR_TEST.limitations: General statistical-learning text, not a claim that the TraderCockpit run is statistically validated or live-tradable.

ACADEMIC_WHITE_SNOOP.citation: Halbert White, A Reality Check for Data Snooping, Econometrica 68(5), 1097-1126 (2000)
ACADEMIC_WHITE_SNOOP.supports: Reusing data for model selection or inference can make a satisfactory result appear by chance rather than by a repeatable effect.
ACADEMIC_WHITE_SNOOP.limitations: Supports the methodological warning; it does not evaluate the SPY or Dow receipt.

ACADEMIC_SULLIVAN_BOOTSTRAP.citation: Sullivan, Timmermann, and White, Data-Snooping, Technical Trading Rule Performance, and the Bootstrap, Journal of Finance 54(5), 1647-1691 (1999)
ACADEMIC_SULLIVAN_BOOTSTRAP.locator: Article title, data-snooping and technical-rule performance study; DOI 10.1111/0022-1082.00163
ACADEMIC_SULLIVAN_BOOTSTRAP.supports: Technical trading-rule results need data-snooping controls when many rules are examined.
ACADEMIC_SULLIVAN_BOOTSTRAP.limitations: Methodological context only; it does not turn a small recorded candidate population into a broad statistical conclusion.

ACADEMIC_TASHMAN_OOS.citation: Len Tashman, Out-of-sample tests of forecasting accuracy: an analysis and review, International Journal of Forecasting 16(4), 437-450 (2000)
ACADEMIC_TASHMAN_OOS.locator: Abstract and sections on fit/test splits, fixed versus rolling origins, single versus multiple test periods; DOI 10.1016/S0169-2070(00)00065-0
ACADEMIC_TASHMAN_OOS.supports: Out-of-sample evaluation has explicit split, origin, window, and test-period design choices; rolling-origin evaluation creates multiple time-ordered test periods.
ACADEMIC_TASHMAN_OOS.limitations: Forecasting-evaluation review; this episode uses its design vocabulary without claiming a walk-forward run occurred here.

ACADEMIC_BERGMEIR_CV.citation: Bergmeir, Hyndman, and Koo, A Note on the Validity of Cross-Validation for Evaluating Autoregressive Time Series Prediction, Computational Statistics and Data Analysis 120, 70-83 (2018)
ACADEMIC_BERGMEIR_CV.locator: Abstract and discussion of serial correlation, non-stationarity, and out-of-sample evaluation; DOI 10.1016/j.csda.2017.11.003
ACADEMIC_BERGMEIR_CV.supports: Time-series evaluation cannot blindly borrow independent-data assumptions; the temporal structure of the evaluation design matters.
ACADEMIC_BERGMEIR_CV.limitations: Autoregressive forecasting paper; it is context for the design question, not a result about this trading engine.

ACADEMIC_NIST_DISTRIBUTION.citation: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, Distribution (Location, Spread and Shape)
ACADEMIC_NIST_DISTRIBUTION.locator: Section 3.1.3.1, distribution characterized by location, spread, and shape
ACADEMIC_NIST_DISTRIBUTION.supports: A distribution describes the scattering of measured outputs around a central value and includes location, spread, and shape.
ACADEMIC_NIST_DISTRIBUTION.limitations: Statistical definition; the episode does not compute a new Dow or SPY distribution.

ACADEMIC_NIST_PERCENTILE.citation: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, Percentiles
ACADEMIC_NIST_PERCENTILE.locator: Section 7.2.6.2, order statistics and percentile definition; 50th percentile is the median
ACADEMIC_NIST_PERCENTILE.supports: Percentiles locate values in an ordered set; the 50th percentile is the median.
ACADEMIC_NIST_PERCENTILE.limitations: Definition only; no percentile is claimed for the small E02 receipt unless a future run computes one.

ACADEMIC_METRIC_ONTOLOGY.citation: QuantConnect, Backtest Statistics; QuantConnect, Warm Up Periods
ACADEMIC_METRIC_ONTOLOGY.locator: Backtest Statistics: profitFactor and profitToMaxDrawdownRatio fields; Warm Up Periods: no trades during warm-up and bar-count warm-up
ACADEMIC_METRIC_ONTOLOGY.supports: The official methodology documentation defines profit factor as total profit divided by total loss, profit-to-maximum-drawdown as total profit/loss divided by maximum closed-trade drawdown, and warm-up as historical data used to prepare indicators before trading. In E02, the source field label trades_per_month is taught as a rate with the displayed unit trades per month.
ACADEMIC_METRIC_ONTOLOGY.limitations: This is an official methodology and metric-ontology receipt, not a peer-reviewed evaluation of the TraderCockpit engine. It defines the teaching vocabulary; the E02 values and the recorded 200/2 lineage inputs remain bound to the private run receipts.

RUN_SPY_PHASE01.locator: phase01_intake fields and candidate gate pointers
RUN_SPY_PHASE01.supports: SPY intake counts and inequalities are read from the hash-bound file.
RUN_SPY_PHASE01.limitations: Does not establish live execution or future performance.

RUN_SPY_PHASE02.supports: The empty later phase and skip note are read from the hash-bound file.
RUN_SPY_PHASE02.limitations: No later SPY return exists in this receipt.

RUN_DOW_PHASE01.supports: The same Dow candidate's in-sample net and PF are read from the hash-bound file.
RUN_DOW_PHASE01.limitations: This is a separate futures lane from SPY.

RUN_DOW_PHASE02.locator: phase02_oos counts and candidate metric pointers
RUN_DOW_PHASE02.supports: Dow later-block counts and the candidate's later metrics are read from the hash-bound file.
RUN_DOW_PHASE02.limitations: This is one later block, not a proof of live performance.

RUN_SPY_LEDGER.locator: candidate lineage.generation_params and lineage.explanation on the bound row
RUN_SPY_LEDGER.supports: The source row records the RSI2 concept, its 200/2 window inputs, and the explicit engine-side exit assumption used by the lesson.
RUN_SPY_LEDGER.limitations: The ledger describes candidate lineage and an assumption; it is not a full execution specification.

RUN_SPY_MANIFEST.supports: The run identity is bound to the saved program and candidate provenance row.
RUN_SPY_MANIFEST.limitations: Manifest metadata does not validate a live fill.

RUN_LIVE_MANIFEST.supports: The current series manifest cross-checks the two E02 branches.
RUN_LIVE_MANIFEST.limitations: It is a copied manifest; the phase JSON hashes remain the primary run receipts.
